title: Working at Redwood: Onboarding, Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is the canonical People Ops reference for working at Redwood. It consolidates high-level guidance on company culture, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks highlights, the hiring and onboarding workflow, and a practical guide to the primary internal tools and access process. Team-level pages provide deeper, role-specific expectations and procedures.

Quick links:
- Roles & ladders
- Benefits summary
- Hiring and interviewing process
- 90-day onboarding checklist
- Internal tools & access requests
- FAQs and escalation contacts

1) Culture and expectations
Redwood is an engineering-driven company focused on production-grade LLM inference. Core behaviors expected of every employee:
- Ship with reliability: prioritize SLOs, testing, and operational readiness.
- Communicate clearly: document decisions and raise risks early.
- Own outcomes: measure impact, follow through, and learn from failures.
- Be inclusive: recruit and collaborate across diverse perspectives.

2) Roles and career ladders (overview)
High-level role families and leveling bands. Consult your manager and the People Ops leveling rubric for detailed criteria and example behaviors.
- Engineering: Software Engineer (IC1-6), Tech Lead, Engineering Manager, Senior Manager, Director.
- Infrastructure & SRE: SRE (IC2-5), Principal SRE, SRE Manager.
- Product & Design: PM1-PM4, PD1-PD4, Group PM.
- Research & Applied ML: R1-R5, Staff / Principal Researchers.
- GTM: Account Exec, Solutions, Customer Success, RevOps (IC and manager tracks).
- People Ops & Finance: TA Partner, People Ops Partner, Finance Ops, Legal Counsel.

Level highlights (examples):
- IC3 (Mid): delivers end-to-end features for a service, mentors juniors, owns code and operational tasks.
- IC4 (Senior): shapes architecture within a service, leads cross-team designs, drives quality improvements.
- IC5 (Staff): leads multi-team efforts, sets technical direction, resolves high-visibility incidents.
- Manager track: Manager 1 leads a small team (3-6), Manager 2 manages managers or large programs.

Promotion process (summary):
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet: impact statements, deliverables, scope growth.
2. Manager collects peer and stakeholder feedback.
3. Calibration committee reviews the packet against the rubric and issues a decision with feedback.
4. People Ops communicates outcomes and next steps.

3) Compensation & benefits (summary)
Redwood provides a competitive total rewards package: base salary, equity grants, benefits, and learning and wellbeing programs. See the benefits portal for plan-level details and eligibility. Key highlights: 
- Health care: medical, dental, vision plans (US vendors; EU/EMEA equivalents where applicable).
- Paid time off: base vacation allowance plus company holidays and discretionary wellness days.
- Family leave: primary caregiver up to 18 weeks paid; secondary caregiver up to 8 weeks (subject to local law).
- Retirement: 401(k) match in the US and country-appropriate retirement options elsewhere.
- Equity: initial option grants with standard vesting (4 years, 1-year cliff) and periodic refreshes.
- Wellbeing: monthly mental health/wellness stipend and access to EAP and coaching.
- Learning & development: annual learning stipend and conference/course reimbursement.
- Perks: home office stipend, commuter benefits, team retreat budgets, flexible hybrid work policy.

Benefits snapshot table (example):
| Category | Typical offering | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Medical | HMO/PPO options (US) | Plans vary by country; see benefits portal |
| Parental Leave | Up to 18 weeks (primary) | Eligibility and notice requirements apply |
| Equity | Stock option grants | Vesting schedule 4y (1y cliff) |
| Retirement | 401(k) match (US) | See Finance for contribution limits |

4) Hiring and interviewing (principles and stages)
Principles: structured interviews, inclusive panels, transparent candidate communications, and timely feedback. Use the role-specific interview kit for scorecards and question banks.
Typical hiring stages:
1. Requisition and scorecard creation (Hiring manager + Recruiter).
2. Sourcing & recruiter screen.
3. Technical or role-specific interviews (2-4 rounds depending on level).
4. Hiring manager interview + team fit conversation.
5. Bar-raiser or cross-functional interview for senior roles.
6. Compensation approval and offer sign-off (People Ops + Finance).
7. Reference checks and background verification.
8. Offer acceptance and onboarding scheduling.

Interviewer rules:
- Use a written scorecard aligned to the role rubric for every interview.
- Provide feedback within 48 hours.
- Prefer diverse interview panels for senior hires.
- Recruiter manages candidate communications and negotiations.

5) Onboarding: first 90 days (concise checklist)
Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Complete offer paperwork and benefits enrollment.
- Submit hardware and software requests via Access Request form.
- Join welcome Slack channels and receive orientation calendar.

Day 1-7:
- People Ops orientation: payroll, benefits, policies, and code of conduct.
- Manager 1:1 to set expectations and the 30/60/90 plan.
- IT provisioning: laptop, Okta SSO, MFA, GitHub, email, and Redwood Console access.
- Assigned security and compliance training modules.

Weeks 2-4:
- Team onboarding: architecture overview, service map, runbooks, and product demo.
- Buddy program: weekly touchpoints with assigned buddy.
- First small contributor task assigned (first PR or documentation update).

Month 1-3:
- 30/60/90 plan reviews and manager check-ins.
- Shadow on-call where applicable and review incident playbooks.
- Attend cross-functional rituals and product planning meetings.

By 90 days:
- Own a small deliverable end-to-end and present a learnings readout.
- Performance check-in with manager to confirm ongoing goals and development plan.

New hire essentials checklist (short):
- Accounts provisioned: Okta, GitHub, Slack, Redwood Console, Buildkite, HR portal.
- SSO & MFA configured.
- Security training completed.
- First PR merged or first operational task completed.
- 30/60/90 plan shared with manager.

6) Internal tools: owners and quick how-to
Primary tools and owners:
- Slack: Communication & incident channels. Owner: GTM & People Ops.
- Confluence: Documentation. Owner: People Ops / Eng Platform.
- GitHub: Source control and PR workflows. Owner: Eng Platform. Use CODEOWNERS and branch protection.
- Buildkite: CI pipelines. Owner: Eng Infra.
- Terraform & IaC repos: Infrastructure management. Owner: Eng Infra.
- Grafana & Honeycomb: Metrics & tracing. Owner: Eng Platform.
- PagerDuty: On-call and escalation routing. Owner: Eng SRE.
- Okta: SSO and identity provider. Owner: Security & Compliance.
- HRIS (Workday/BambooHR): Payroll and time-off. Owner: People Ops.
- Greenhouse: ATS for requisitions and interviews. Owner: Talent Acquisition.

Access request flow:
1. Open the Access Request form (Confluence > People Ops > Access Requests).
2. Attach manager approval and justification.
3. Tool owner provisions access within 3 business days for standard requests; expedited provisioning available for new hires via People Ops.

Common onboarding tips and commands:
- Git: follow repo README and branch naming convention feature/<ticket>-short-desc.
- CI: check Buildkite pipeline status; add logs to PRs when asking for re-runs.
- Observability: run team-name-overview dashboard to check SLOs prior to deploy.

7) FAQs and escalation points
- Payroll questions: payroll@redwood.com (People Ops).
- Security incidents: security@redwood.com and Security Incident form.
- Access & provisioning delays: people-ops@redwood.com.
- On-call escalations: follow PagerDuty runbooks and contact Eng SRE on-call.

8) Related policies and deeper references
- Company Code of Conduct (Confluence link).
- Remote & Hybrid Work policy (Confluence link).
- Compensation & Promotions rubric (People Ops page).
- Security & Compliance playbook (Confluence link).

9) Ownership and maintenance
Document owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel). Review cadence: annual review and ad-hoc updates for major policy or legal changes. To request edits, open a Confluence edit proposal or email people-ops@redwood.com.

Appendix: 30/60/90 template (example)
- 30 days: Learn systems, ship first small change, meet key collaborators.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a small feature or operational story, present a systems readout.
- 90 days: Deliver cross-functional work and propose at least one process or tooling improvement.

End of document. For team-specific ladders, manager calibration guides, and legal benefits forms, see the related pages listed above.
